voiceGuide: Guide the child through digging up 6 dinosaurs by tapping rocks, learning facts about each one, and answering quiz questions. Celebrate each discovery and quiz success. Use actual dinosaur names in all per-dinosaur narrations.

welcome.text: Welcome to Dino Dig Adventure! Let's dig up some dinosaurs!

dig_start.text: Tap the rock to crack it open! Keep tapping!

dig_2.text: Keep going! The rock is cracking!

reveal.text: You found something new! Amazing discovery!

quiz_time.text: Quiz time! Let's see what you learned!

quiz_correct.text: That's right! You really know your dinosaurs!

next_dino.text: Great job! Let's find the next dinosaur!

victory.text: You discovered all 6 dinosaurs! You're a Dino Expert!

try_again.text: Want to dig again? Let's go!

reveal.text: You found a Stegosaurus! Amazing discovery!

learn1.text: Stegosaurus had 17 bony plates on its back that could get up to 2 feet tall!

learn2.text: Its brain was only the size of a walnut, one of the smallest brains compared to body size.

learn3.text: It had 4 sharp spikes on its tail called a thagomizer to fight off predators!

quiz_time.text: What were the spikes on Stegosaurus's tail called?

quiz_correct.text: That's right! Stegosaurus had a thagomizer on its tail!

quiz_wrong.text: Good try! Stegosaurus had 4 sharp tail spikes called a thagomizer.

reveal.text: You found a Triceratops! Amazing discovery!

learn1.text: Triceratops means three-horned face. It had two big horns above its eyes and one on its nose!

learn2.text: Its huge neck frill could be over 3 feet wide and was used for protection and showing off.

learn3.text: Triceratops had up to 800 teeth arranged in groups called batteries that were constantly replaced!

quiz_correct.text: That's right! Triceratops means three-horned face!

quiz_wrong.text: Good try! Triceratops means three-horned face.

reveal.text: You found a Pteranodon! Amazing discovery!

learn1.text: Pteranodon wasn't actually a dinosaur, it was a flying reptile called a pterosaur!

learn2.text: Its wingspan could reach 23 feet wide, that's wider than a giraffe is tall!

learn3.text: Pteranodon had a long pointed crest on the back of its head that helped it steer while flying!

quiz_time.text: What type of creature was Pteranodon?

quiz_correct.text: That's right! Pteranodon was a flying reptile called a pterosaur!

quiz_wrong.text: Good try! Pteranodon was a flying reptile called a pterosaur.

reveal.text: You found a Tyrannosaurus Rex! Amazing discovery!

learn1.text: T-Rex had the strongest bite of any land animal ever. It could crush bones with 12,800 pounds of force!

learn2.text: Despite its tiny arms, each arm could still curl about 430 pounds!

learn3.text: T-Rex could smell prey from miles away thanks to huge olfactory bulbs in its brain!

quiz_time.text: What was T-Rex's most powerful feature?

quiz_correct.text: That's right! T-Rex had a bone-crushing bite!

quiz_wrong.text: Good try! T-Rex's most powerful feature was its bone-crushing bite.

reveal.text: You found a Brachiosaurus! Amazing discovery!

learn1.text: Brachiosaurus could reach 85 feet high, as tall as a 4-story building, thanks to its long neck!

learn2.text: It weighed about 62 tons, that's as heavy as 10 African elephants!

learn3.text: Unlike most dinosaurs, its front legs were longer than its back legs, giving it a giraffe-like stance!

quiz_correct.text: That's right! Brachiosaurus could reach as tall as a 4-story building!

quiz_wrong.text: Good try! Brachiosaurus could reach 85 feet high, as tall as a 4-story building.

reveal.text: You found an Oviraptor! Amazing discovery!

learn1.text: Oviraptor means egg thief, but scientists now know it was guarding its own eggs, not stealing them!

learn2.text: It had a parrot-like beak perfect for cracking tough food like shellfish and seeds.

learn3.text: Oviraptor had a colorful crest on its head like a cassowary, and may have had feathers too!

quiz_correct.text: That's right! Oviraptor means egg thief!

quiz_wrong.text: Good try! Oviraptor means egg thief.
